chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who authorized her affair to a man, so she said, 'Marry me to so-and-so.' He said, 'I will not marry you until you bear witness for me that your affair is in my hand.' So she bore witness for him. He said during the marriage to the one who proposed to her, 'O so-and-so, upon you is such and such.' He said, 'Yes.' He said to the people, 'Bear witness that that is for her with me, and that I have married her myself.' The woman said, 'No, and there is no prestige, and my command is not except in my own hand, and I did not authorize my command to you except due to embarrassment from speaking (myself).' He said: 'She is snatched away from him, and his head is struck (shamed).'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Nu'man, from Abu Al-Subah Al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman delegates her marriage to a man and he marries her off to someone else without her specific consent?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between general marriage authority (wilayah) and specific consent (rida), establishing that a woman's delegation to a matchmaker does not imply unconditional surrender of her choice. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates that if the man marries her to someone else without her explicit agreement to that specific match, he loses his authority and is subject to physical correction (dharb al-ra's) as a penalty for his presumption. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that a woman's silence or modesty (hayā') in accepting a proposal is not equivalent to full consent, protecting her agency within the marital contract.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether, from IBn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a woman who authorised her matter to a man, so she said, ‘Get me married to so and so’. So he said, ‘I will not get you married until you bear witness for me that your matter is in my hands’. So she bore witness for him. So he said during the marriage to the one who had proposed to her, ‘O so and so, upon you is such and such (a debt)’. He said, ‘Yes’. So he said to the group of people who were present, ‘That is present for her with me, and that I have married her myself’. So the woman said, ‘No, and there is no prestige, and my command is not except in my own hands, and I had not authorised my command to you except due to embarrassment from the speaking (myself)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would be snatched away from him, and he should be given a (knock on the) head (to be shamed)’.
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, from Abu Abdullahasws – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“About the case of a woman who appoints a man to form her marriage with so and so and he says, ‘I will do so only if you testify that I am your attorney;’ she testifies for him and at the time of ceremony he says to the man who has proposed marriage, ‘O so and so you owe such and such amount’ and he says, ‘Yes, I agree.’ He (her attorney) says to people, ‘Bear witness that this amount for her is on me and I give her in marriage to myself.’ She then says, ‘No, it is not an honor. The control of my affairs is in my own hand and I have not appointed you as the person in charge of my affairs. It was only because of not to verbally be embarrassed before people.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is removed from her. He deserves only a headache.’”
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
